subject: Throughput sizing follow-up - FinEx latency & tokens/sec profile

From: Alex Kim <alex.kim@finex.com>

Subject: Re: Discovery notes - throughput / latency targets

Neha / Redwood team - thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap from our side and a couple of clarifying questions so we can get a sizing recommendation from you: 

- Target SLO: 95th percentile end-to-end latency <= 300ms for streaming responses (clients need token-by-token streaming). P50 ideally < 120ms.
- Peak traffic: up to ~250 QPS during market open windows (bursts typically 10-20 minutes).
- Steady-state: ~40 QPS outside peak windows.
- Typical request: ~120 tokens generated on average; however ~5% of requests can be long (up to 1024 tokens) for audit/analysis.
- Concurrent sessions: ~1200 active sessions in peak, but concurrency per instance depends on batching and streaming constraints.

Questions:
1) Can you provide a rough tokens/sec or GPUs recommendation for our model profile (we're evaluating a ~13B quantized open model)?
2) Do you recommend Dedicated capacity for predictable latency, or can hosted inference meet these SLOs?
3) We will need KV-cache reuse for repeated user context - what's the expected impact on throughput?

Also attaching our basic traffic histogram (will send separately). Happy to schedule a 30m follow-up - Priya and I are available Tue/Wed next week.

Thanks,
Alex
Director, Platform Engineering
FinEx Trading

From: rafael.mendes@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Discovery notes - throughput / latency targets

Alex / Neha - quick SE-level notes and B.O.E. numbers to get the conversation started. These are conservative back-of-envelope figures; final sizing will depend on the exact model variant, quantization, sequence-length distribution, and whether you can tolerate some batching-induced latency versus strict single-request streaming.

Assumptions:
- Model: open-13B quantized (int8-ish) with standard autoregressive decode.
- Target tail latency: P95 <= 300ms streaming (token-by-token).
- Average tokens/request: 120 (5% up to 1024).
- KV-cache reuse assumed 30% in B.O.E. (gives effective lower compute per request).

Rough throughput (single A100-class GPU equivalent)
- Streaming (strict token-by-token, minimal batching): ~60-100 tokens/sec sustained (depend on seq len & kernel ops).
- Non-streaming batched generation (allowing batching to fill for 50-100ms): ~250-400 tokens/sec.

Sizing guidance (purely illustrative):
- Steady-state 40 QPS x 120 tokens = 4800 tokens/sec. At 300 tokens/sec effective per GPU (batched path), ~16 GPUs. If using streaming path (60 tps), ~80 GPUs (not practical).
- Peak 250 QPS x 120 tokens = 30,000 tokens/sec. At 300 tps per GPU => ~100 GPUs. At streaming path rates (60 tps) => ~500 GPUs.

Implications:
- If streaming token-by-token at P95 < 300ms is mandatory for the entire traffic volume, Dedicated capacity is strongly recommended for predictable tail latency and to reduce cross-tenant noisy-neighbor variance.
- Common production pattern: route highest-SLO traffic to Dedicated (or reserved pool) and route bulk non-latency-sensitive traffic through batched hosted endpoints with autoscaling. Batching + KV-cache brings huge token/sec gains.
- For mixed workloads, a hybrid approach (Dedicated reserved for critical routes + hosted for steady/background) usually reduces total GPU needs and cost while meeting SLOs.

Next steps I can take this afternoon:
- Produce a table with three scenarios (all-hosted, hybrid, all-dedicated) and estimated GPU counts for steady and peak windows.
- Call out assumptions (batching latency budget, cache hit ratio, quantization profile).

Neha / Marissa - I'll send the draft sizing table back by EOD if Alex/FinEx can confirm distribution numbers and whether burst durations are 10-20m as called out.

- Rafael Mendes
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com
